# `hk`: kernels, types, values

The language: what `import hk` gives a kernel author. A kernel body is traced once per set of constexprs; [the language](../language.md) says how it is written, this page what each name is. The namespaces have pages of their own: [hk.math](hk.math.md), [hk.arch](hk.arch.md), [hk.lds](hk.lds.md), [hk.group](hk.group.md), [hk.collective](hk.collective.md), [hk.comm](hk.comm.md), [hk.placement](hk.placement.md); the shipped kernels are [hk.ops](hk.ops.md), the templates [hk.templates](hk.templates.md), the checker [hk.check](hk.check.md), the profiler [hk.profile](hk.profile.md), the per-arch facts [hk.target](hk.target.md).

## Kernels

### `hk.kernel`

```python
hk.kernel(fn=None, *, arch: Optional[str] = None, warps: int = 1, grid=None, name: Optional[str] = None, max_vgprs: Optional[int] = None, min_occupancy: Optional[int] = None, max_occupancy: Optional[int] = None, defines: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, noalias: bool = False, preload: bool = False, resident: bool = False, placement=None)
```

*Changed after 0.8.0*: new parameter `max_occupancy`

Mark a function as a tile kernel. See the module docstring for the
parameter rules. `resident=True`: every workgroup must be on the GPU at
once (a kernel that waits on its own workgroups); a launch that cannot be
is refused with ResourceError rather than deadlocking. `placement`: which
XCD runs which workgroup -- None, "auto" or an hk.Placement
(hk.dsl.placement, docs/design/placement-pass.md).

### `hk.func`

```python
hk.func(fn)
```

A device helper: traced inline where it is called, with its `for`, `if`
and `while` rewritten like a kernel's.

### `hk.Kernel`

```python
class hk.Kernel(fn: Callable, *, arch: Optional[str] = None, warps: int = 1, grid: Optional[Callable] = None, name: Optional[str] = None, max_vgprs: Optional[int] = None, min_occupancy: Optional[int] = None, max_occupancy: Optional[int] = None, defines: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, noalias: bool = False, preload: bool = False, resident: bool = False, placement=None)
```

A tile kernel. Call it to launch; `trace`, `source` and `build` stop
earlier, and need no GPU.

#### `Kernel.arch (property)`

The arch it builds for: `arch=` if given, else
`hk.target.current_arch()` ($HK_ARCH, else the GPU).

#### `Kernel.trace`

```python
Kernel.trace(self, **const_overrides: Any) -> TracedKernel
```

Run the body once into an hk module and run the passes over it.
No GPU, no compiler.

#### `Kernel.source`

```python
Kernel.source(self, scaffold: str = 'pybind', **const_overrides: Any) -> str
```

The generated HipKittens C++. Readable on purpose -- it is the
artifact you take to /kernel-resource-check when something spills.

#### `Kernel.with_defines`

```python
Kernel.with_defines(self, src: str) -> str
```

*Surface*: an escape hatch, used only within its boundary: #define NAME value knobs and A/B variants; never overridden to splice or rewrite C++.

`src` with this kernel's preprocessor definitions ahead of it, and
its occupancy cap (`max_occupancy`) at the top of its body.

#### `Kernel.build`

```python
Kernel.build(self, **const_overrides: Any)
```

Generate and compile. Returns a runtime.Build, which carries the
per-instantiation resource numbers as well as the .so.

The compile step gates on ScratchSize and register spills: a kernel that
spills is not slow here, it is *wrong*, because include/rdna3 hand-manages
s_waitcnt. A spilling build raises rather than being returned.

Needs hipcc but not a GPU, which is what makes the whole development
loop runnable on a machine with no Radeon in it.

#### `Kernel.build_flags`

```python
Kernel.build_flags(self, traced: TracedKernel) -> Tuple[str, ...]
```

*Surface*: an escape hatch, used only within its boundary: tests and probes; not hk.ops kernels.

hipcc flags of this kernel's builds beyond the target's.

#### `Kernel.preloaded`

```python
Kernel.preloaded(self) -> Kernel
```

This kernel with `preload` set: its own builds, the same body.

#### `Kernel.compile`

```python
Kernel.compile(self, **const_overrides: Any)
```

Generate, compile and load. Returns the loaded extension module.

#### `Kernel.placed`

```python
Kernel.placed(self, placement=None) -> Kernel
```

This kernel with `placement` (default: the analysis's cluster
placement) installed: its own name (a suffix for the placement),
traces and builds, the same body.

#### `Kernel.placement_choice`

```python
Kernel.placement_choice(self, *tensors: Any, **const_overrides: Any)
```

hk.dsl.placement.choose for these tensors: whether
placement="auto" launches the cluster placement, and why.

#### `Kernel.resident_capacity`

```python
Kernel.resident_capacity(self, **const_overrides: Any) -> int
```

How many workgroups of this kernel the current GPU holds at once:
its CUs times the workgroups a CU fits by registers and by LDS (the
smaller), from the build's own resource report.

#### `Kernel.specialize`

```python
Kernel.specialize(self, **const_overrides: Any) -> Kernel
```

A view of this kernel with different constexpr defaults.

Memoized, and that is not an optimization detail. A fresh Kernel has
empty trace / build / module caches, so calling `specialize()` on every
invocation -- which is what a wrapper like `rmsnorm(x, eps=...)`
naturally does -- re-traces the body and re-resolves the extension
module on every launch. Measured on the W7900D that was ~3.5 ms of
Python in front of a 0.5 ms kernel: rmsnorm and layernorm came out
flat in the tensor size, which is the signature of a fixed host cost
rather than a slow kernel.

The cheaper surface is to pass the constexpr to the call itself --
`k(x, o, EPS=eps)` -- which uses the caches directly and makes no
object at all. specialize() is for handing a configured kernel to
something that will call it many times.

### `hk.TracedKernel`

```python
class hk.TracedKernel(name: str, arch: str, warps: int, consts: Dict[str, Any], tensors: List, module: ir.Module, grid: Tuple = (), analysis=None, plan=None, logical_grid: Tuple = ())
```

One specialization of a kernel, traced and lowered: its hk module and
what the module boundary needs to know about it.

#### `TracedKernel.threads (property)`

warps x the target's wave: the workgroup's size.

#### `TracedKernel.tensors`

```python
TracedKernel.tensors(self) -> List[Param]
```

The tensor parameters, in order, with their types.

#### `TracedKernel.written_tensors`

```python
TracedKernel.written_tensors(self) -> List[str]
```

The tensors the kernel stores into, in declaration order.

#### `TracedKernel.cpp`

```python
TracedKernel.cpp(self, includes) -> str
```

The kernel's HipKittens C++ body, with `includes`; `Kernel.source()`
is the whole translation unit.

#### `TracedKernel.dump`

```python
TracedKernel.dump(self) -> str
```

The module as MLIR, values named as the C++ names them: `%ld1`
here is `ld1` in `cpp()`. Printed from a copy, renamed by the
translation's own naming, so the two cannot disagree.

### `hk.Tensor`

The annotation for a tensor parameter: `x: hk.Tensor[hk.bf16]`.

`hk.Tensor[hk.bf16, "system"]` (or "device") is a *scoped* tensor: memory
another GPU ("system") or another XCD of this GPU ("device") reads or
writes while the kernel runs -- a peer's buffer, a mailbox. Every load,
store and atomic through it carries the scope, and hk.comm.signal /
hk.comm.wait take only scoped tensors (see hk.comm for why the scope is
the tensor's and not the access's).

### `hk.Constexpr`

Marks a constexpr parameter, with its type if you like:
`EPS: hk.Constexpr[float] = 1e-6`. Every keyword-only parameter is a
constexpr whether or not it says so -- the marker documents it, which
matters when a kernel has a dozen knobs -- and a positional one is a
constexpr when it is annotated so.

## Types

### `hk.RT`

```python
hk.RT(dtype: DType, rows: int, cols: int, layout: str = 'row', frag=None) -> RegTileType
```

A register tile type: kittens::rt<T, rows, cols, layout>. `frag`,
(rows, cols), names the matrix-core fragment where it is not 16x16; left
out, the hk-fragments pass sets it on the operand tiles that need one.

### `hk.RS`

```python
hk.RS(dtype: DType, rows: int, cols: int, run: int = 8) -> RegTileType
```

A register strip type: kittens::rs<T, rows, cols, run>.

The layout for kernels that stream rows -- a norm, a softmax -- rather
than feed WMMA: lane l owns, of every row, the runs of `run` contiguous
columns starting at j*wave*run + l*run (wave = 32 on gfx1100, 64 on
gfx950; `hk.arch.target().wave`), so a bf16 run of 8 is one 16-byte
access and nothing is held twice. `cols` is a whole number of wave*run
chunks: 256 or 512 columns at run 8, so 512 fits both. A strip loads and stores (element coordinates only, the element
type converting on the way), maps, reduces along rows (a butterfly that
leaves the answer in every lane) and columns, broadcasts its col_vec and
row_vec, and fills by column. Its row_vec has the strip's own column
layout: a weight vector loads with the same accesses as the rows it
scales.

### `hk.ST`

```python
hk.ST(dtype: DType, rows: int, cols: int, count: int = 1) -> SharedTileType
```

An LDS tile type; count > 1 is a multi-buffer.

### `hk.SV`

```python
hk.SV(dtype: DType, length: int, count: int = 1) -> SharedVecType
```

An LDS vector type.

### `hk.col_vec`

```python
hk.col_vec(tile: RegTileType) -> RegVecType
```

One value per *row* of `tile`: what `t.sum(axis=1)` gives.

### `hk.row_vec`

```python
hk.row_vec(tile: RegTileType) -> RegVecType
```

One value per *column* of `tile`.

### `hk.DType`

```python
class hk.DType(name: str, bits: int, cpp: str, kind: str) -> None
```

An element type: `hk.bf16`, `hk.fp16`, `hk.fp32`, `hk.i32`, `hk.i8`,
`hk.fp8e4m3`, `hk.fp8e5m2`. `name` is hk's spelling, `cpp` the
HipKittens one, `bits` and `bytes` its size.

## Control flow

### `hk.range`

```python
hk.range(start, stop=None, step=None, *, unroll: int = 1) -> DynRange
```

A loop the kernel runs at run time, even over constant bounds.

`unroll` becomes `#pragma unroll N`. Leave it at 1 unless measured:
unrolling a body that already fills the register file is how a kernel
starts to spill, and a spill here is a wrong answer, not a slow one.

### `hk.range_constexpr`

```python
hk.range_constexpr(start, stop=None, step=None)
```

A loop unrolled at trace time; its bounds must be Python ints.

### `hk.if_`

```python
hk.if_(cond, *, opaque: bool = False, uniform: bool = False) -> Iterator[None]
```

A region that runs only where `cond` holds.

`opaque=True` hides the condition from the optimizer (an empty asm that
claims to modify it), so the branch survives even when it folds to a
constant -- the tool for keeping two live sets apart. `uniform=True`
declares the condition the same in every warp (see `hk.uniform`): the
region may then hold barriers.

### `hk.scope`

```python
hk.scope() -> Iterator[None]
```

An always-taken region that is a boundary for the register allocator:
one VGPR and a never-taken branch, and two live sets that no longer have
to be held at once.

### `hk.uniform`

```python
hk.uniform(cond)
```

`cond`, declared the same in every warp of the workgroup -- made of the block index,
scalar loads every warp makes, constexprs and the tensors' extents, never of warp_id or a
lane's value. A branch on it (`if hk.uniform(bid < 160):` or `hk.if_(c, uniform=True)`) may
hold workgroup operations -- barriers, group copies -- as every warp takes it or none does:
the role dispatch of a persistent kernel. So may a runtime loop on it, `while hk.uniform(t <
n):`, every warp running the same iterations: a work queue's loop over `hk.comm.claim`. The declaration is the author's; a condition that
differs between warps deadlocks at the first barrier inside.

## Functions

### `hk.cdiv`

```python
hk.cdiv(a, b)
```

Ceiling division: of ints at trace time, of device Ints in the kernel,
of tensor extents in a grid lambda.

### `hk.min`

```python
hk.min(a, b)
```

Of ints, of device Ints, or elementwise of tiles and vectors.

### `hk.max`

```python
hk.max(a, b)
```

Of ints, of device Ints, or elementwise of tiles and vectors.

### `hk.zeros`

```python
hk.zeros(ty, *, into=None)
```

A register tile or vector of type `ty` filled with 0, or `into=` an
existing one: `acc = hk.zeros(hk.RT(hk.fp32, 16, 64))`.

### `hk.full`

```python
hk.full(ty, value: float, *, into=None)
```

A register tile or vector of type `ty` filled with `value`.

### `hk.neg_infty`

```python
hk.neg_infty(ty, *, into=None)
```

A register tile or vector of type `ty` filled with -inf: a running
max's start.

### `hk.rand`

```python
hk.rand(ty, seed, offset, row_stride, *, into=None) -> Tile
```

Uniform [0, 1) draws into an fp32 tile: element (r, c) is the draw
`triton.language.rand(seed, offset + r * row_stride + c)` makes, bit for
bit -- Philox4x32-10 with Triton's constants and conversion -- so a
dropout written here keeps exactly the elements Triton's keeps.

### `hk.transpose`

```python
hk.transpose(t: Tile, *, into=None) -> Tile
```

Transpose by relabelling: mirrored shape, opposite layout, no data
moved beyond the register shuffle.

### `hk.transpose_sep`

```python
hk.transpose_sep(t: Tile, *, into=None) -> Tile
```

Transpose keeping the layout. Moves data; needs separate registers.

### `hk.broadcast_row`

```python
hk.broadcast_row(ty: RegTileType, vec: Vec) -> Tile
```

A tile whose every row is vec[row].

### `hk.broadcast_col`

```python
hk.broadcast_col(ty: RegTileType, vec: Vec) -> Tile
```

A tile whose every column is vec[col]: element (r, c) is vec[c], for
a row_vec `vec` (one value per column).

### `hk.as_vec`

```python
hk.as_vec(vec: Vec, tile: RegTileType, *, uniform: bool = False) -> Vec
```

Re-attach a register vector to a tile of another shape, where the C++
types are the same: element type, length and layout.

### `hk.mma`

```python
hk.mma(variant: str, a, b, acc: Tile, *, into=None) -> Tile
```

`acc + A x B` on the WMMA unit. The variant is decided by the layouts
you have; the wrong one is how a kernel buys eight ds_read_u16 per base
tile instead of two ds_read_b128.

Scaled operands (`Tile.scaled`) make it gfx950's block-scaled MFMA
(v_mfma_scale_f32_16x16x128_f8f6f4): `hk.mma("mma_ABt", a.scaled(sa),
b.scaled(sb, fmt="fp4"), acc)` is acc + (sa . A)(sb . B)^T for A (M, K) and
B (N, K) fp8 e4m3 row tiles (FP4 in the fp8 container with fmt="fp4"), K a
multiple of 128, element (r, k) of A counting as A[r][k] *
2^(sa[r][k // 32] - 127), acc an fp32 col tile (M, N). Both operands are
scaled, and the variant is mma_ABt.

### `hk.load_w4`

```python
hk.load_w4(ty, qw: Global, s: Global, zs: Global, n0, k0, *, group: int = 128, into=None) -> Tile
```

*Surface*: a format primitive: hk's own int4 layout (hk.ops.w4a16's repack).

Rows n0.. and columns k0.. of W, dequantized from 4-bit codes into a
bf16 row-layout tile: element (n, k) is q * s - zs, q being nibble k % 8
of row n's word k // 8 (int32 [N, K/8], interleaved [N/16][K/32][16][4]),
s and zs the group's scale and zero-times-scale `s[n][k // group]`,
`zs[n][k // group]` (bf16 [N, K/group]). The layout
`hk.ops.w4a16.repack_*` writes. The tile is a whole number of 32-column
chunks and k0 a multiple of 32, and of the tile's width when the group
spans it.

### `hk.coord`

```python
hk.coord(b: Scalar = 0, d: Scalar = 0, r: Scalar = 0, c: Scalar = 0, *, unit: str = 'tile') -> Coord
```

A (batch, depth, row, col) index. `unit` is "tile" (C++ `coord<RT>`)
or "element" (`coord<>`); picking the wrong one reads the wrong memory
without any diagnostic, which is why it is in the type.

### `hk.tile_coord`

```python
hk.tile_coord(b: Scalar = 0, d: Scalar = 0, r: Scalar = 0, c: Scalar = 0) -> Coord
```

A (batch, depth, row, col) index in tiles: row r is rows
[r*R, (r+1)*R) for a load of an R-row tile. `x[hk.tile_coord(...)]`.

### `hk.elem_coord`

```python
hk.elem_coord(b: Scalar = 0, d: Scalar = 0, r: Scalar = 0, c: Scalar = 0) -> Coord
```

A (batch, depth, row, col) index in elements: what `x.at[r, c]`
builds. Strips index only this way.

## MX and FP4 (gfx950)

### `hk.load_mx_scales`

```python
hk.load_mx_scales(src: Global, rows: int, kblocks: int, row0, kb0, *, into: MxScales = None, layout: str = 'ocp', group_rows: int = 0, loose: bool = False) -> MxScales
```

*Surface*: a format primitive: E8M0 scales of gfx950's scaled MFMA (v_mfma_scale_f32_16x16x128_f8f6f4)'s operands; a new layout is a layout= value, not a new op.

Rows row0.. and 32-wide blocks kb0.. of an E8M0 scale tensor (uint8, one
byte a row and block: [R, K/32], the OCP MX layout -- or packed, i32, as
hk.mx.pack_scales lays them out: one coalesced dword a lane per 64
rows and K step) for an fp8 operand tile of `rows` rows and `kblocks * 32`
columns. gfx950 only.

`layout="aiter_gate_up"` / `"aiter"`: AITER's shuffled MoE weight scales
(uint8 [E * group_rows, K/32], `shuffle_scale(is_guinterleave=True)`, with
and without gate_up) -- the scales of a `load_fp4_frags` tile of the same
rows: row0 the tile's first row in [E * group_rows], base tiles alternating
gate and up with "aiter_gate_up". AITER scales are kept as loaded (fmt 2:
the MFMA's opsel picks the byte; kb0 a multiple of 8 when kblocks > 4).
`loose` (byte scales): a register a 16-row tile and K step, the byte as
loaded (fmt 1). Both leave nothing for the VALU to do with a loaded
scale, so its wait sits at the MFMA instead of right after the load --
the packed form's byte insertion waited there, draining every load
issued before it (K1 c8).

### `hk.load_fp4_frags`

```python
hk.load_fp4_frags(ty, src, row0, kc0, *, group_rows: Optional[int] = None, gate_up: bool = False, into=None) -> Tile
```

*Surface*: a format primitive: AITER's pre-shuffled MXFP4 MoE weights only.

Rows row0.. and 128-wide K steps kc0.. of AITER's shuffled MXFP4 MoE weights (gfx950,
`shuffle_weight(is_guinterleave=True)`; src uint8 [E * group_rows, K/2], the packed bytes)
as an FP4 operand, `w.scaled(sw, fmt="fp4")` in `hk.mma`. `ty` is an fp8 e4m3 row tile of
16x128 fragments -- the container: each fragment's first four dwords hold the FP4 operand, the
rest stay undefined. With `gate_up` (a stage-1 gate|up weight) the base tiles alternate the
gate and up halves of 16-row block (row0 % group_rows) // 16 + i // 2, so gate column j and up
column j of the product land in the same lanes.

`src` may instead be an LDS tile of raw AITER weight bytes (fp8-typed, a row a 16-row block
with gate|up rows interleaved, 1 KB a 128-wide K step: the [E * N/16 * 2, K/2 * 16] view of
the weights, brought in by a group load): fragment (i, s) is then its row row0 + i and 1 KB
chunk kc0 + s, and `group_rows` / `gate_up` do not apply.

### `hk.mx_quant_store`

```python
hk.mx_quant_store(src: SharedTile, q: Global, s: Global, row0, col0) -> None
```

*Surface*: to be merged into a G1 composition (hk.mx) (DSL-surface migration S10).

MX-quantize an LDS tile's rows and store them -- the epilogue that hands a GEMM's output
to an MXFP8 consumer without a separate quant pass. Every thread of the workgroup takes
(row, 32-column group) pairs of `src` (bf16 or fp32: store it, then barrier, first). For each
group it computes AITER's E8M0 exponent exactly, e = ceil(log2(amax / 448)) from amax's bits.
It writes the FP8 e4m3 values to q[row0 + r, col0 + 32 g ..] and the scale byte to `s`:
a uint8 `s` gets AITER's 32-row layout (hk.mx.aiter_scales of q's [R, K/32], K/32 padded to
8), an int32 `s` the packed layout hk.load_mx_scales reads ([ceil(R/64), K/128 * 64],
hk.mx.pack_scales; rows past q's last get the unit scale, as pack_scales pads them). The
result is bit-identical to hk.mx.quant followed by hk.mx.aiter_scales or hk.mx.pack_scales.

### `hk.copy_mx_scales`

```python
hk.copy_mx_scales(dst: MxScales, src: MxScales) -> None
```

*Surface*: deprecated, removed in the release after the last call from outside the repository is migrated, at most two minor releases after its deprecation; use MxScales.copy(into=).

Deprecated: `src.copy(into=dst)`. dst = src, E8M0 scales copied register to register.

### `hk.mma_ABt_mx`

```python
hk.mma_ABt_mx(a: Tile, b: Tile, acc: Tile, sa: MxScales, sb: MxScales, *, into=None, a_fmt: str = 'fp8', b_fmt: str = 'fp8', sa_at=(0, 0), sb_at=(0, 0)) -> Tile
```

*Surface*: deprecated, removed in the release after the last call from outside the repository is migrated, at most two minor releases after its deprecation; use hk.mma with Tile.scaled operands.

Deprecated: `hk.mma("mma_ABt", a.scaled(sa, fmt=a_fmt, at=sa_at),
b.scaled(sb, fmt=b_fmt, at=sb_at), acc)`, the same instruction.

## Strips: a C++ expression, iota, a raw MFMA (gfx950)

### `hk.map_cpp`

```python
hk.map_cpp(expr: str, *args, dtype: Optional[DType] = None, name: str = 'map') -> Tile
```

*Surface*: an escape hatch, used only within its boundary: an intrinsic or instruction hk has no op for, or another kernel's exact instruction sequence; not index arithmetic, selects, bit ops or float expressions the operators can write; never in a template.

An elementwise C++ expression over strips (gfx950): element (r, c) of the result is `expr`
with `x0`, `x1`, ... bound to element (r, c) of each strip argument -- or to the argument
itself for an `Int` or a Python int -- converted to `dtype` (default: the strips' one dtype;
strips of fp32 and i32 together must say it).

For what the operators cannot say and a kernel must reproduce bit for bit: bit manipulation,
a fused multiply-add, one particular instruction. E.g. the biased exponent of the smallest
power of two >= x:

    e = hk.map_cpp("((__builtin_bit_cast(int, x0) >> 23) & 0xFF)"
                   " + ((__builtin_bit_cast(int, x0) & 0x7FFFFF) != 0)", x, dtype=hk.i32)

The strips have one shape and run; strips and result are fp32 or i32 (convert a 16-bit strip
with `.to` first). The expression is one C++ expression, compiled as written -- with
floating-point contraction off, so `a * b + c` is two roundings and a fused multiply-add is
spelled `__builtin_fmaf` -- no `;` or braces, and the compiler, not hk, checks it.

### `hk.iota`

```python
hk.iota(ty) -> Tile
```

*Surface*: to be merged into hk.lane_coords(type)[1] (alias kept) (DSL-surface migration S6).

An i32 strip of type `ty`'s shape whose element (r, c) is c: each element's own column, for
index arithmetic (hk.map_cpp, load_elems / store_elems) and per-column choices (gfx950).

### `hk.mfma_strip`

```python
hk.mfma_strip(kind: str, a: Tile, b: Tile, acc: Tile) -> Tile
```

*Surface*: to be merged into hk.mma on Tile.as_fragment views (DSL-surface migration S9).

One raw MFMA on strip registers (gfx950), for a result that must match another kernel's
MFMA bit for bit. "f32_16x16x4": `acc` (hk.RS(fp32, 1, 256, 4): lane l's four values are C
rows 4 (l // 16) + i, column l % 16) + A B^T over K = 4, where lane l of `a` and `b`
(hk.RS(fp32, 1, 64, 1)) holds A[l % 16][l // 16] and B[l % 16][l // 16] --
v_mfma_f32_16x16x4_f32, nothing reordered. Returns the new accumulator.

## Workgroup placement (multi-XCD GPUs)

Which XCD runs which workgroup: `hk.kernel(placement=...)` takes None (the hardware's order), `"auto"` (the cluster placement where the policy takes it) or an `hk.Placement`. Outputs are bitwise the unplaced kernel's; only the order changes. On a part with one L2 (gfx1100) every placement is the identity. `hk.arch.xcd_count()` is the XCD count it deals over, `Kernel.placed()` / `Kernel.placement_choice()` the placed kernel and the policy's decision, `hk.placement.analyze` / `hk.placement.choose` the analysis and the policy, `python -m hk.check --placement` checks a launch covers its grid exactly once ([check](../check.md#which-xcd-runs-which-workgroup---placement), [design](../design/placement-pass.md)).

### `hk.Placement`

How a kernel's workgroups are numbered.

Placement.cluster()            one sharing cluster an XCD at a time; the key from
                               `analyze` (the dominant read's), or `key=` digits
                               the analysis cannot see (an index read from memory)
Placement.chunked(chunk, tail) block_idx.x only, within each (y, z) slice and
                               with the grid as it is: rounds of `xcds * chunk`
                               consecutive ids an XCD (a GEMM's xcd_chunk, whose
                               y is the split-K share); chunk="even" is an
                               eighth of the axis an XCD
Placement.none()               the identity

`tail` is what happens past the last whole round: "stay" (in round-robin
order, what the hand-written GEMM remaps did) or "spread" (dealt as
contiguous ranges, balanced to one). chunk 0 is contiguous ranges outright.

### `hk.Digit`

A grid axis whole (`kind` "whole"), or one digit of it: `axis // radix`
("div") or `axis % radix` ("mod"). `radix` is an int, a tensor extent
spelled "tensor.dim" (`Digit.of("x", "mod", "k.depth")`: the KV heads of
a (B, H_KV, N, D) `k`), or a host expression of extents and constexprs.

Made with `hk.Digit.of(axis, kind="whole", radix=None)`: `hk.Digit.of("z")`, `hk.Digit.of("x", "mod", 8)`. A `Placement.cluster(key=...)` names its sharing key with these where the analysis cannot see it (an index read from memory).

## Dtypes

| name | bits | C++ | kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hk.bf16` | 16 | `bf16` | float |
| `hk.fp16` | 16 | `half` | float |
| `hk.fp32` | 32 | `float` | float |
| `hk.i32` | 32 | `int` | int |
| `hk.i8` | 8 | `int8` | int |
| `hk.fp8e4m3` | 8 | `fp8e4m3` | float |
| `hk.fp8e5m2` | 8 | `fp8e5m2` | float |

fp8 is a matrix operand where the target has an fp8 matrix instruction: gfx950's MFMA (plain, and block-scaled through `hk.mma` with `Tile.scaled` operands, which may also be FP4) and gfx1201's WMMA. i8 is a WMMA operand on gfx1100 (`v_wmma_i32_16x16x16_iu8`, an i32 accumulator) and a storage type elsewhere. `hk.mx` has the MX scale layouts and torch references. `hk.DTYPES` maps the names to these.

## Device values

What a kernel body computes with. They are made by loads, `hk.zeros` and friends, never constructed directly; their methods are the language. A method ending in `_` writes the value in place; `into=` names the value an operation writes.

**Operators** (`n` a Python number, `a`, `b` values of the column's kind; a vector broadcasts against a tile along the axis it was reduced from):

| operator | `Tile` | `Vec` | `Int` | `Bool` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `a + b` | yes | yes | yes |  |
| `n + a` | yes | yes | yes |  |
| `a - b` | yes | yes | yes |  |
| `n - a` | yes | yes | yes |  |
| `a * b` | yes | yes | yes |  |
| `n * a` | yes | yes | yes |  |
| `a / b` | yes | yes | refused |  |
| `n / a` | yes | yes |  |  |
| `a // b` | refused | refused | yes |  |
| `a % b` | refused | refused | yes |  |
| `-a` | yes | yes | yes |  |
| `abs(a)` | yes | yes |  |  |
| `a += b (also -= *= /=)` | yes | yes | yes (rebinds) |  |
| `a @ b` | yes |  |  |  |
| `a < b (<= > >= == !=)` |  |  | yes |  |
| `a & b, a \| b, a ^ b` |  |  |  | yes |
| `~a` |  |  |  | yes |
| `v[:, None], v[None, :]` |  | yes |  |  |

`acc += a @ b.T` is one matrix-core instruction into `acc` (the variant follows from the transposes); `t.sum(axis=1)` and friends are lazy reductions that `+=`, `max_` or `.value()` land.

### `hk.Tile`

A register tile: kittens::rt<T, rows, cols, layout>.

#### `Tile.dtype (property)`

The element dtype.

#### `Tile.sum`

```python
Tile.sum(self, axis: int = 1, *, lanes: Optional[str] = None, xor: Optional[Sequence[int]] = None, times: "Optional['Tile']" = None) -> Reduction
```

The sum along `axis`: 1 (default) along each row, one value per row (a col_vec); 0 along each column (a row_vec). Lazy: `v = t.sum()` makes the vector, `acc += t.sum()` accumulates into one, and `.value(into=v)` writes an existing one.

#### `Tile.max`

```python
Tile.max(self, axis: int = 1, *, lanes: Optional[str] = None, xor: Optional[Sequence[int]] = None) -> Reduction
```

The max along `axis`: 1 (default) along each row, one value per row (a col_vec); 0 along each column (a row_vec). Lazy: `v = t.max()` makes the vector, `m.max_(t.max())` folds into one (the online max), and `.value(into=v)` writes an existing one.

#### `Tile.first_lane`

```python
Tile.first_lane(self) -> Int
```

*New after 0.8.0*

Lane 0's first element of this i32 strip, as a scalar (v_readfirstlane, gfx950). Uniform
across the workgroup when every wave holds the same value -- one LDS word read after a
barrier -- so it may drive hk.uniform branches (an early exit decided by one wave).

#### `Tile.lane_strip`

```python
Tile.lane_strip(self, run: int = 8) -> Tile
```

*New after 0.8.0*

This tile's registers as a 1-row strip, lane by lane (gfx950): no data moves. Lane l's
elements, in the tile's per-lane order (a matrix-core tile: its fragments row by row of
fragments, each fragment's elements in order; a strip: its rows, chunks and runs), become
the lane's runs of `run`, chunk after chunk -- so `hk.map_cpp`, the group reductions and
`store_elems` work on an MMA result where it sits. `hk.lane_coords(tile, run)` says which
row and column of the tile each element is. 32-bit elements.

#### `Tile.run_xor`

```python
Tile.run_xor(self, mask: int) -> Tile
```

*New after 0.8.0*

Each element from another element of its lane's run (gfx950): element e of a run becomes
element e ^ `mask` of the same run, a register move. A rotary pair's partner, when the pair
sits in one run (an MMA result taken by `lane_strip`).

#### `Tile.lane_gather`

```python
Tile.lane_gather(self, lanes: Tile) -> Tile
```

Each element from another lane (gfx950): element (r, c) of lane l is the same run element
of lane `lanes[r, c]` (an i32 strip of this strip's shape, 0..63) -- ds_bpermute, one an
element. A lane group's small-matrix work (a 4x4 Sinkhorn's row and column sums) without
LDS. 32-bit elements.

#### `Tile.group_max`

```python
Tile.group_max(self, cols: int, *, lanes: str = 'seq', xor: Optional[Sequence[int]] = None) -> Tile
```

A strip's rows reduced over groups of `cols` columns (a lane group's runs: an MX group is
32 columns of a run-8 strip), the group's max in every element. `lanes` and `xor` state the
order, as for `sum(axis=1, ...)`; the offsets are 1 .. cols / run / 2 (neighbouring lanes),
or as many other distinct powers of two up to 32: the group is then a lane's run and those of
lanes l ^ (a sum of the offsets). A 32x32 matrix-core result taken as a strip
(`lane_strip(16)`) holds 32 rows of a column in lane l's run and lane l ^ 32's:
`group_max(32, xor=(32,))`. gfx950.

#### `Tile.group_min`

```python
Tile.group_min(self, cols: int, *, lanes: str = 'seq', xor: Optional[Sequence[int]] = None) -> Tile
```

As `group_max`, the minimum.

#### `Tile.group_sum`

```python
Tile.group_sum(self, cols: int, *, lanes: str = 'seq', xor: Optional[Sequence[int]] = None) -> Tile
```

As `group_max`, the sum, in the stated order.

#### `Tile.min`

```python
Tile.min(self, axis: int = 1, *, lanes: Optional[str] = None, xor: Optional[Sequence[int]] = None) -> Reduction
```

The min along `axis`: 1 (default) along each row, one value per row (a col_vec); 0 along each column (a row_vec). Lazy: `v = t.min()` makes the vector, and `.value(into=v)` writes an existing one.

#### `Tile.prod`

```python
Tile.prod(self, axis: int = 1, *, lanes: Optional[str] = None, xor: Optional[Sequence[int]] = None) -> Reduction
```

The product along `axis`: 1 (default) along each row, one value per row (a col_vec); 0 along each column (a row_vec). Lazy: `v = t.prod()` makes the vector, and `.value(into=v)` writes an existing one.

#### `Tile.to`

```python
Tile.to(self, dtype: DType, *, into=None) -> Tile
```

Change the element type, keeping shape and layout (kittens::copy).

#### `Tile.bitcast`

```python
Tile.bitcast(self, dtype: DType, *, into=None) -> Tile
```

The same registers read as another element type of the same width (fp32 <-> i32,
bf16 <-> fp16 ...): no instruction, unlike `.to`. E.g. an i32 accumulator started at the
bits of 1.5 * 2^23 read as fp32 is 1.5 * 2^23 + S exactly for |S| < 2^22 -- the int ->
float convert of an iu8 product, folded away (experiment 1's c7 needed a C++ rewrite).

#### `Tile.T (property)`

This tile transposed, as an MMA operand (`acc += a @ b.T`) or for `.value()`, which makes the transposed tile.

#### `Tile.left_fill_`

```python
Tile.left_fill_(self, idx, value=0.0, *, into=None)
```

Set the elements in columns < idx to `value` (default 0), in place or `into=` a copy: the mask for a ragged last tile. `idx` may be a device Int. Strips take left_fill_ and right_fill_ only.

#### `Tile.right_fill_`

```python
Tile.right_fill_(self, idx, value=0.0, *, into=None)
```

Set the elements in columns >= idx to `value` (default 0), in place or `into=` a copy: the mask for a ragged last tile. `idx` may be a device Int. Strips take left_fill_ and right_fill_ only.

#### `Tile.upper_fill_`

```python
Tile.upper_fill_(self, idx, value=0.0, *, into=None)
```

Set the elements in rows < idx to `value` (default 0), in place or `into=` a copy: the mask for a ragged last tile. `idx` may be a device Int. Not on strips.

#### `Tile.lower_fill_`

```python
Tile.lower_fill_(self, idx, value=0.0, *, into=None)
```

Set the elements in rows >= idx to `value` (default 0), in place or `into=` a copy: the mask for a ragged last tile. `idx` may be a device Int. Not on strips.

#### `Tile.triu_`

```python
Tile.triu_(self, idx, value=0.0, *, into=None)
```

Keep the upper triangle from diagonal `idx`, the rest set to `value` (default 0), in place. Not on strips.

#### `Tile.tril_`

```python
Tile.tril_(self, idx, value=0.0, *, into=None)
```

Keep the lower triangle from diagonal `idx`, the rest set to `value` (default 0), in place. Not on strips.

#### `Tile.as_fragment`

```python
Tile.as_fragment(self, ty, *, fmt: str = 'fp8') -> Tile
```

*New after 0.8.0*

This i32 strip's registers as a matrix-core operand fragment, no data moved (gfx950):
lane l's elements, in the strip's per-lane order (rows, chunks, runs), become lane l's
dwords of `ty` -- the inverse of `lane_strip` on 32-bit data. For operands gathered with
`load_elems(runs=True)` from a layout no tile load knows, or kept in LDS as words.

`ty` is the 16x128 fp8 e4m3 row tile (`hk.RT(hk.fp8e4m3, 16, 128)`) a block-scaled MMA
reads (`Tile.scaled`). fmt="fp8": eight dwords a lane, a strip of 1 x 512 at run 4 -- run 0
the K step's 16 bytes at K 16 (l / 16) .., run 1 those at 64 + 16 (l / 16) .., of row
l % 16: the fragment a tile load makes. fmt="fp4": four dwords a lane, a strip of 1 x 256
at run 4 -- lane l's 32 FP4 values being row l % 16, columns 32 (l / 16) .. + 32 -- in the
FP4 container (its upper half undefined).

#### `Tile.as_scales`

```python
Tile.as_scales(self) -> MxScales
```

*New after 0.8.0*

This i32 strip (1 x 64, run 1) as loose E8M0 scales of a 16x128 operand, no data moved
(gfx950): lane l's element, the byte in bits 0..7, is the scale of row l % 16, block
l / 16 -- `Tile.scaled` takes it.

#### `Tile.scaled`

```python
Tile.scaled(self, scales: MxScales, *, fmt: str = 'fp8', at=(0, 0)) -> Scaled
```

*New after 0.8.0*

This operand with its E8M0 block scales, for gfx950's block-scaled MFMA:
`hk.mma("mma_ABt", a.scaled(sa), b.scaled(sb, fmt="fp4"), acc)`. `fmt` is "fp8"
(e4m3) or "fp4" (the FP4 container `hk.load_fp4_frags` fills). `at` = (tile, step):
the scales may cover more than the operand -- its 16-row base tile i and 128-wide step s
take the scales' tile i + tile and step s + step (a 32-row block's two-step AITER
dwords, loaded once, feeding two token tiles over two steps).

#### `Tile.as_operand`

```python
Tile.as_operand(self, dtype: Optional[DType] = None, *, into=None) -> Tile
```

This accumulator's registers read as an MFMA operand: no data
moves across lanes (gfx950).

`self` is a col-layout tile in an accumulator fragment -- an MFMA
result, or its cast to bf16. Each lane holds a column and four rows
at a time; read as a stride-4 operand fragment (32x32 -> 16x32/4,
16x16 -> 32x16/4), its rows are the reduction index in another order,
and an MMA whose other operand has the same stride (hk-fragments
lays it out so) computes the same product. So with the scores kept
transposed, `o_t += v.T @ p_t.as_operand(bf16)` is P·V straight off
the softmax, with no reshuffle across lanes. `dtype` converts an
fp32 accumulator on the way (to nearest even); a 16-bit one is read
as it is.

#### `Tile.subtile`

```python
Tile.subtile(self, rows: int, index: int) -> Tile
```

Rows [index*rows, (index+1)*rows) of this tile, as a tile of
`rows` rows that is the same registers: an op writing into it writes
this tile (include/cdna4's subtile_inplace). `index` is a Python int
-- a runtime one would index the register file. Not an LDS load's
destination: load into the whole tile.

#### `Tile.make_causal`

```python
Tile.make_causal(self, value: float = 0.0, *, into=None, transposed: bool = False)
```

*Surface*: deprecated, removed in the release after the last call from outside the repository is migrated, at most two minor releases after its deprecation; use Tile.tril_(0, v) / Tile.triu_(0, v).

Deprecated: `tril_(0, value)` (`triu_(0, value)` with `transposed=True`), which takes
any diagonal. A copy of this tile with the elements above the diagonal set to `value`
(below it with `transposed=True`), or into `into`; this tile is unchanged.

#### `Tile.swap_halves`

```python
Tile.swap_halves(self, span: Optional[int] = None, *, negate_first: bool = False, into=None)
```

*Changed after 0.8.0*: new parameters `span`, `negate_first`

A strip with the two halves of each `span`-column segment of its rows exchanged (span
None: the whole row): in a segment's first half column c takes column c + span/2, in
its second c - span/2. `negate_first` negates what lands in the first half -- NeoX's
rotate_half, [x1 | x2] -> [-x2 | x1] (`rotate_half(span)` is this). Strips only, on the
wave64 port (gfx950). The halves are whole chunks apart (a register swap) or 8, 16 or 32
lanes apart (a DPP row_ror:8, a v_permlane16_swap, a v_permlane32_swap): a whole row of
one chunk or of an even number of them, or a head of `span` columns -- a 128-column head
at eight bf16 a lane is 16 lanes, its halves eight apart.

#### `Tile.rotate_half`

```python
Tile.rotate_half(self, span: int, *, into=None)
```

NeoX's rotate_half on each `span`-column segment of a strip's rows:
[x1 | x2] -> [-x2 | x1], one head of `span` columns a segment --
`swap_halves(span, negate_first=True)`.

### `hk.Vec`

A register vector: one value per row (col kind) or column (row kind)
of the tile it came off.

#### `Vec.max_`

```python
Vec.max_(self, r: Reduction) -> Vec
```

Fold `t.max(axis=...)`, or another partial max (a vector), into this
vector: the online max. A reduction's NaN and signed-zero rules either
way (docs/language.md); `maximum` is the elementwise op.

#### `Vec.min_`

```python
Vec.min_(self, r: Reduction) -> Vec
```

Fold `t.min(axis=...)` into this vector: the running min.

#### `Vec.any_ne`

```python
Vec.any_ne(self, other: Vec) -> Int
```

Wave-level: did any entry differ from `other`. A uniform branch.

#### `Vec.any_above`

```python
Vec.any_above(self, other: Vec, threshold: float) -> Int
```

Wave-level: did any entry exceed `other`'s by more than
`threshold`. A uniform branch. The online softmax's lazy rescale:
keep taking exp2 against a stale running max until the new one is
more than `threshold` (log2 units) above it.

#### `Vec.maximum`

```python
Vec.maximum(self, o, *, into=None)
```

#### `Vec.swap_halves`

```python
Vec.swap_halves(self, span: Optional[int] = None, *, negate_first: bool = False, into=None)
```

*Changed after 0.8.0*: new parameters `span`, `negate_first`

A strip with the two halves of each `span`-column segment of its rows exchanged (span
None: the whole row): in a segment's first half column c takes column c + span/2, in
its second c - span/2. `negate_first` negates what lands in the first half -- NeoX's
rotate_half, [x1 | x2] -> [-x2 | x1] (`rotate_half(span)` is this). Strips only, on the
wave64 port (gfx950). The halves are whole chunks apart (a register swap) or 8, 16 or 32
lanes apart (a DPP row_ror:8, a v_permlane16_swap, a v_permlane32_swap): a whole row of
one chunk or of an even number of them, or a head of `span` columns -- a 128-column head
at eight bf16 a lane is 16 lanes, its halves eight apart.

#### `Vec.rotate_half`

```python
Vec.rotate_half(self, span: int, *, into=None)
```

NeoX's rotate_half on each `span`-column segment of a strip's rows:
[x1 | x2] -> [-x2 | x1], one head of `span` columns a segment --
`swap_halves(span, negate_first=True)`.

### `hk.Global`

A global tensor parameter, 4D (b, d, r, c).

`x[idx]` is a view at a coordinate; `x.at[r, c]` builds an element
coordinate and `x.tile[r, c]` a tile one, left-padding with zeros.

#### `Global.batch (property)`

The tensor's extent along axis 0 of (batch, depth, rows, cols), a device Int.

#### `Global.depth (property)`

The tensor's extent along axis 1, a device Int.

#### `Global.rows (property)`

The tensor's rows (axis 2), a device Int. A 2-D tensor is (rows, cols).

#### `Global.cols (property)`

The tensor's columns (axis 3), a device Int.

#### `Global.dtype (property)`

The element dtype the parameter was annotated with.

#### `Global.at (property)`

Element indexing: `x.at[r, c]` (or `[b, d, r, c]`) is a View at that element; a load reads the tile that starts there.

#### `Global.tile (property)`

Tile indexing: `x.tile[r, c]` is a View at tile (r, c) of the tile type the load names.

#### `Global.load_elems`

```python
Global.load_elems(self, idx: Tile, dtype: Optional[DType] = None, *, runs: bool = False, row=None) -> Tile
```

*Changed after 0.8.0*: new parameters `runs`, `row`

Element by element at computed indices (gfx950): element (r, c) of the result is element
`idx[r, c]` of this tensor, counted flat (rows over batch and depth, at the row stride),
converted to `dtype` (fp32 or i32; default fp32, i32 for an i32 tensor). An index below
zero or past the tensor reads 0 -- a table lookup with a fallback, a key table's slots.
`idx` is an i32 strip (hk.map_cpp computes one).

`runs=True`: the kernel says each lane's run comes from consecutive elements from its first
element's index, aligned to the run's bytes; the run is one load (1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 k bytes),
read as 0 if that first index is out of range -- a lane's 4 fp32 in one 16-byte load, not
four gathered ones. `row`: as store_elems.

#### `Global.store_elems`

```python
Global.store_elems(self, val: Tile, idx: Tile, *, runs: bool = False, row=None) -> None
```

*Changed after 0.8.0*: new parameter `row`

Element by element at computed indices (gfx950): element (r, c) of `val` (an fp32 or
i32 strip), converted to this tensor's type, to element `idx[r, c]` (flat, as
load_elems). An index below zero or past the tensor writes nothing: -1 masks an element
out. Two elements to one index race.

`runs=True`: the kernel says each lane's run goes to consecutive elements from its first
element's index, aligned to the run's bytes; the run is one store (1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 k
bytes), masked by that first index -- 8 fp8 values in one 8-byte store, not eight.

`row` (a device Int): the indices count from that row, whose base is formed in 64 bits and
whose range is the one row -- a tensor past a 32-bit offset (a paged cache of many GB)
addressed a row (block) at a time.

#### `Global.post_elems`

```python
Global.post_elems(self, val: Tile, idx: Tile, tag, *, runs: bool = False, bf16: bool = False) -> None
```

Tagged mailbox pairs, an element at a time (gfx950): element (r, c) of `val` (fp32 or i32
strip) and `tag` go to pair `idx[r, c]` of this scoped int32 tensor (int32 elements 2 i,
2 i + 1) as one 8-byte store of its scope; an index below zero posts nothing. No drain --
the value travels with its tag -- so a hand-off between CTAs is one store and, on the
other side, one poll (dsv41_mono's Mailbox; hk.comm.post for one scalar).

`runs=True`: each lane's run goes to consecutive pairs from its first element's index (the
lane's other indices are not read), two pairs a 16-byte store; the run is a whole number of
pairs of pairs. `bf16=True` (with runs): two values a pair, as bf16 -- the TOP HALVES of the
fp32 values, so they must already be bf16 values (rounded by the caller); the pairs from a
run's first index are then run / 2.

#### `Global.take_elems`

```python
Global.take_elems(self, idx: Tile, tag, dtype: Optional[DType] = None, *, timeout_s: float = 2.0, runs: bool = False, bf16: bool = False) -> Tile
```

The other side of post_elems: element (r, c) is the value of pair `idx[r, c]` once its tag
is `tag`; every element's pair is loaded with the tensor's scope, and all are re-loaded
(s_sleep between) while any is stale. An index below zero is ready at 0. `dtype`: fp32
(default) or i32. After `timeout_s` the kernel traps (0: never) -- a lost post is an error,
not a hang. `runs=True` / `bf16=True`: the layout post_elems wrote with them.

#### `Global.gather`

```python
Global.gather(self, tile, ids, at=None, *, count=None, col=0, div=None, into=None) -> Tile
```

*Surface*: `div=`: deprecated, removed in the release after the last call from outside the repository is migrated, at most two minor releases after its deprecation; use hk.RowIndex(div=).

Rows by index: tile row r is row `ids[at + r]` of this tensor (rows flattened over
batch and depth), from column `col` -- `ids` an `hk.RowIndex`, which also says how an
index names a row (`div`), or an int32 tensor and `at` (and `count`). An index outside the
tensor, or a position at or past `count` (default: all of `ids`), reads zeros -- the
padding a MoE sort fills its index list with costs no branch. `div=` here is deprecated:
`hk.RowIndex(ids, at, div=...)`.

#### `Global.scatter`

```python
Global.scatter(self, value: Tile, ids, at=None, *, count=None, col=0, sort_topk: Optional[int] = None, add: bool = False, staged: Optional[int] = None) -> None
```

*Changed after 0.8.0*: new parameter `staged`

*Surface*: `sort_topk=`: deprecated, removed in the release after the last call from outside the repository is migrated, at most two minor releases after its deprecation; use hk.RowIndex(sort_topk=).

*Surface*: `staged=`: deprecated, removed in the release after the last call from outside the repository is migrated, at most two minor releases after its deprecation; use an index staged by Group.stage_rows.

*Surface*: `add=`: atomic scatter-add, in no fixed order: not for a route that promises determinism.

Rows by index: tile row r goes to row `ids[at + r]`, from column `col` -- `ids` an
`hk.RowIndex`, or an int32 tensor and `at` (and `count`). An index outside the tensor, or
a position at or past `count`, writes nothing. Two rows naming one row race. With an
index of AITER's MoE sort ids (`RowIndex(..., sort_topk=k)`: token | choice << 24) this
tensor is [k * M, ...] choice-major -- row r goes to row choice * M + token, and padding
(token >= M) nowhere.

`add=True` adds the rows atomically instead (an fp32 or bf16 global; bf16 adds element
pairs, gfx950's global_atomic_pk_add_bf16). With sort ids the tensor is then [M, ...] and
every choice of a token adds into its row: the top-k reduce, in no fixed order -- the
result varies run to run by the rounding of the adds.

An index staged in LDS by `g.stage_rows(ix, N, keep_choice=True)` is read there: a global
index load is a vmcnt wait, which on gfx950 retires every load and store issued before
it, in order -- in an epilogue between K loops, the next loop's whole prefetch and this
epilogue's own earlier stores (K1 k1-prefill c36). `sort_topk=` and `staged=` here are
deprecated: they are `hk.RowIndex`'s and `g.stage_rows`'.

#### `Global.type (property)`

The value's hk type (`RegTileType`, `RegVecType`, ...).

### `hk.View`

A global at a coordinate: what a load reads and a store writes.

#### `View.load`

```python
View.load(self, tile, *, into: "Optional['Value']" = None, bounded=False, period: Optional[int] = None)
```

Global -> register tile or vector. The element type converts on the
way in, for free. `bounded=True` predicates rows past the global's
last (they read zero and touch no memory); `bounded=n`, an int or a
device Int, also predicates rows at or past `n` counted from the
tile's first -- for a tile whose rows end before the tensor's.

`period` (a strip, unbounded): column c of the strip reads column
c % period from the view's -- `period` values repeated along it, as
one token's angles under each of its heads.

#### `View.store`

```python
View.store(self, value, *, bounded=False) -> None
```

Register tile or vector -> global. `bounded` as for load: True
drops rows past the global's last, `n` also rows at or past `n`.

#### `View.load_scalar`

```python
View.load_scalar(self, *, invariant: bool = False) -> Int
```

One int32 element -> a wave-uniform scalar (a page index, a length).

`invariant`: nothing writes the element while the kernel runs (a page
table, the sequence lengths), so on gfx950 it is a scalar load
(s_load_dword), counted on lgkmcnt -- not a vector load whose wait
also waits out every copy issued before it.

#### `View.store_scalar`

```python
View.store_scalar(self, vec: Vec) -> None
```

One entry of a *uniform* register vector -> one element.

#### `View.atomic_add`

```python
View.atomic_add(self, value: Tile) -> None
```

Add an fp32 tile into this float global, element by element,
atomically: the reduction for partials in different workgroups.

#### `View.atomic_add_scalar`

```python
View.atomic_add_scalar(self, value) -> Int
```

One int32 atomic add per warp; the element's value before it, in
every lane. W warps that call it add W times.

#### `View.atomic_max_scalar`

```python
View.atomic_max_scalar(self, value) -> Int
```

One int32 atomic max per warp; the value before it.

#### `View.atomic_min_scalar`

```python
View.atomic_min_scalar(self, value) -> Int
```

One int32 atomic min per warp; the value before it.

#### `View.atomic_or_scalar`

```python
View.atomic_or_scalar(self, value) -> Int
```

One int32 atomic or per warp; the value before it (a set of flags: bit w = workgroup w).

#### `View.atomic_and_scalar`

```python
View.atomic_and_scalar(self, value) -> Int
```

One int32 atomic and per warp; the value before it.

#### `View.atomic_xor_scalar`

```python
View.atomic_xor_scalar(self, value) -> Int
```

One int32 atomic xor per warp; the value before it.

#### `View.atomic_exch_scalar`

```python
View.atomic_exch_scalar(self, value) -> Int
```

One int32 atomic exchange per warp: stores `value`, returns the value before it (a
lock's take, a slot's claim). W warps that call it exchange W times.

### `hk.SharedTile`

An LDS tile, or a stack of them (`As[i]` picks one).

#### `SharedTile.load_elems`

```python
SharedTile.load_elems(self, idx: Tile, dtype: Optional[DType] = None, *, runs: bool = False) -> Tile
```

*Changed after 0.8.0*: new parameter `runs`

Element by element from this fp32 LDS tile (gfx950): element (r, c) of the result is
element `idx[r, c]` (row-major, through the tile's swizzle) -- fp32, or its bits as i32 with
dtype=hk.i32; below zero or past the tile, 0. A CTA's own exchange between warps without a
round trip to global memory (whose drain would also wait out every load in flight). Another
warp's writes need hk.arch.barrier(drain=True) between.

`runs=True`: the kernel says each lane's run (a multiple of 4) is consecutive elements from
16-byte-aligned indices; each 4 is one 16-byte read (b32 reads of a lane's 4 consecutive
elements conflict 4 ways across the wave). Index flat into a tile 16 columns wide: a wider
one lays every 16th element a subtile (1 KB) on, on the same banks.

#### `SharedTile.store_elems`

```python
SharedTile.store_elems(self, val: Tile, idx: Tile) -> None
```

Element by element into this fp32 LDS tile (gfx950): val's element (r, c) (fp32, or i32
bits) to element `idx[r, c]` (row-major); below zero or past the tile, nothing. Before
another warp reads it: hk.arch.barrier(drain=True). A bf16 tile takes the fp32 value
rounded to bf16 (round to nearest even) -- an MMA operand built element by element, read
back with `.load` / `.subtile(...).load`.

#### `SharedTile.atomic_add_elems`

```python
SharedTile.atomic_add_elems(self, val: Tile, idx: Tile) -> None
```

*New after 0.8.0*

Element by element, atomically (gfx950): val's element (r, c), an i32, is added to element
`idx[r, c]` of this fp32 LDS tile taken as an i32 (ds_add_u32); below zero or past the tile,
nothing. Every element to one index lands: a histogram's counts. Read the counts with
load_elems(..., i32) after hk.arch.barrier(drain=True).

#### `SharedTile.subtile`

```python
SharedTile.subtile(self, rows: int, cols: int, row: Scalar = 0, col: Scalar = 0) -> SharedTile
```

A rows x cols window, indexed in units of itself; a view, so the
swizzle still applies and loads still vectorise.

#### `SharedTile.load`

```python
SharedTile.load(self, tile: RegTileType, *, wait: bool = True, into=None) -> Tile
```

LDS -> register tile. `wait=False` leaves the reads in flight; the
tile must then be named in hk.lds.wait_for before it is read.

#### `SharedTile.store`

```python
SharedTile.store(self, value: Tile) -> None
```

Register tile -> LDS.

#### `SharedTile.granules`

```python
SharedTile.granules(self, name: str = 'gr') -> Granules
```

*Surface*: an escape hatch, used only within its boundary: the same as hk.Granules'.

Factor this tile's addressing into swizzle_bytes/16 registers, so a
loop reading many fragments holds those and not one address each.

#### `SharedTile.type (property)`

The value's hk type (`RegTileType`, `RegVecType`, ...).

### `hk.MxScales`

*New after 0.8.0*

E8M0 block scales of an fp8 operand tile, in the lanes the scaled MFMA
reads them from (`load_mx_scales`). An operand takes them with
`Tile.scaled`.

#### `MxScales.copy`

```python
MxScales.copy(self, *, into: MxScales) -> MxScales
```

*New after 0.8.0*

`into` = these scales, register to register -- how a one-stage loop body hands
the next K-tile's prefetched scales to the current set. Returns `into`.

#### `MxScales.type (property)`

The value's hk type (`RegTileType`, `RegVecType`, ...).

### `hk.Scaled`

*New after 0.8.0*

An MX operand: an fp8 e4m3 row tile (FP4 in its container with fmt="fp4") and its E8M0
scales, made by `Tile.scaled`. `hk.mma("mma_ABt", a.scaled(sa), b.scaled(sb), acc)` is
gfx950's block-scaled MFMA; nothing else takes one.

### `hk.RowIndex`

*New after 0.8.0*

Which rows a gather, a scatter or a gathered LDS copy moves: row r of the tile is named by
`ids[at + r]`, an int32 global, for positions below `count` (default: all of `ids`) -- and
how such an index names a row:

- plain: it is the row;
- `div=k`: the row is `ids[at + r] // k` (a MoE's top-k, its sorted list counting
  (token, choice) pairs); for a gather;
- `sort_topk=k`: AITER's MoE sort ids, token | choice << 24, padding token >= M. A gather or
  a gathered copy reads the token's row; a scatter writes row choice * M + token of a
  [k * M, ...] tensor, and with add=True adds into the token's row.

Positions at or past `count`, padding and indices outside the tensor read zero and write
nothing. `g.stage_rows(ix, rows)` copies [at, at + rows) into LDS and returns the staged
index the copies then read there (no vmcnt wait for an index). Made in the kernel body; no
instruction of its own.

#### `RowIndex.offset`

```python
RowIndex.offset(self, n) -> RowIndex
```

The same index from position at + n (a later tile of the same block). A staged
index stays staged: [at, at + n + the tile's rows) must lie inside what was staged.

#### `RowIndex.staged`

```python
RowIndex.staged(self, rows: int, *, keep_choice: bool = False) -> RowIndex
```

This index as `g.stage_rows(self, rows, keep_choice=...)` stages it, without the copy:
for code written before the place that stages it (a loop body's copies, defined above
the loop). A consumer still refuses it until a `stage_rows` has made that copy.

### `hk.Int`

A wave-uniform 32-bit integer: an index, an extent, a loop counter.

Python's operators build device arithmetic; `//` and `%` are C++'s
truncating division and remainder, which agree with Python's on the
non-negative values an index takes.

#### `Int.type (property)`

The value's hk type (`RegTileType`, `RegVecType`, ...).

### `hk.Bool`

A comparison's answer: steers an `if`, or combines with & | ~.

#### `Bool.to_int`

```python
Bool.to_int(self) -> Int
```

1 where true, else 0, as an Int.

#### `Bool.type (property)`

The value's hk type (`RegTileType`, `RegVecType`, ...).

### `hk.Coord`

A (b, d, r, c) index, in tiles or in elements.

#### `Coord.unit (property)`

"tile" or "element".

#### `Coord.type (property)`

The value's hk type (`RegTileType`, `RegVecType`, ...).

## Runtime, errors and the rest

### `hk.VerifyError`

The kernel is wrong or unbuildable. Never downgrade one of these.

### `hk.CompileError`

Common base class for all non-exit exceptions.

### `hk.ResourceError`

A kernel that must not be used. Raised, never warned about.

### `hk.Build`

```python
class hk.Build(key: str, module_name: str, so_path: Path, source_path: Path, log_path: Path, kernels: List[KernelResources], cached: bool) -> None
```

One compiled artifact and everything used to judge it.

#### `Build.report`

```python
Build.report(self) -> str
```

One line per instantiation: vgpr, occupancy, LDS, scratch, spills
(KernelResources.line). `python -m hk.check` reports the same with
the occupancy LDS allows.

### `hk.get_target`

```python
hk.get_target(arch: str)
```

Look up a target by gfx name or by the GPU_TARGET name common.mk uses.

### `hk.TARGETS`

The known targets by gfx name, `hk.target.Target` records: see [hk.target](hk.target.md).

### `hk.detect_arch`

```python
hk.detect_arch() -> Optional[str]
```

The local GPU's gfx name, or None. Cached: probing costs a subprocess
and the answer cannot change within a process.

### `hk.torch_op`

```python
hk.torch_op(kernel, *, ns: str = 'hk', name: str = '', **const_overrides)
```

Build, load and return `torch.ops.<ns>.<name>`.

Memoised on (ns, name): the second call in a process returns the same op
rather than re-registering it, which torch refuses with "Tried to register
an operator with the same name twice".

By default it is registered over a device-only code object
(hk.runtime.codeobj): the same schema and checks, without compiling
libtorch's headers -- 1.1-1.5 s a kernel on the pod where this
registration takes 15 (tools/hk-bench/compile_time.py), and the same
time a layer inside vLLM's decode graphs. HK_TORCH_OP=library builds the
libtorch registration below instead.

### `hk.attention`

```python
hk.attention(q, k, v, *, causal: bool = False, scale: Optional[float] = None, out=None)
```

Flash attention forward, (B, H, N, D) bf16, MHA or GQA.

The operand layout is `F.scaled_dot_product_attention`'s, so a framework
that already calls torch can be redirected without reshaping. What this
takes and what it does not is `_why`; it raises rather than falls back,
because a silent fallback inside an explicit `hk.attention` call is how a
20 TFLOPs path gets mistaken for a 64 TFLOPs one.

Ragged N is fine in both directions: the last Q block backs up to end at
n_q and recomputes the overlap (idempotent -- a query row's output depends
on that row alone), and the last KV block backs up and masks the rows it
does not own. So on gfx1100 n_q must be at least Q_TILE (192) and n_kv at
least KV_BLOCK (32). On gfx950 this runs hk.ops.attn_cdna, whose loads
are bounded: any non-empty length. head_dim is 64 or 128 on both.

**Per architecture** ([audit](../dx/api-consistency.md)):

| | gfx1100 (RDNA3) | gfx950 (CDNA4) |
|---|---|---|
| shape | n_q >= 192 (one Q tile) and n_kv >= 32 (one KV block) | any non-empty length |
| head_dim | 64 or 128 | 64 or 128 |
| numerics | dense online softmax | lazily rescaled softmax (threshold 8): same math, different bits |

## Tools

- `hk.check(fn, reference, inputs)`, `python -m hk.check`: correctness, resources and timing in one call: [hk.check](hk.check.md), [docs/check.md](../check.md).
- `hk.profile(fn, inputs)`, `python -m hk.profile`: why it runs at that speed -- counters, the thread trace, the main loop's instructions and a verdict: [hk.profile](hk.profile.md), [docs/profile.md](../profile.md).
